 Medium

 Print Picture Credit: X Music composer Anirudh Ravichander has reportedly decided to take a break from his professional commitments following his wedding to businesswoman Kavya Maran. According to the latest reports the composer may resume work only in January 2027. Anirudh Ravichander reportedly takes a break until January 2027
 As per a report by Valai Pechu, Anirudh is expected to take a break and could begin his next work schedule with the teaser of Kamal Haasan's upcoming film ‘Sandiyar’. The film is also expected to enter full-fledged production around the same time. However, it must be mentioned that Anirudh has not made any official announcement about taking a break or his return to work. Anirudh Ravichander and Kavya Maran tie the knot
 Anirudh and Kavya reportedly tied the knot on November 11, 2026, in a simple self-respect marriage ceremony. The couple is said to have exchanged pendants instead of following elaborate traditional wedding rituals. Anirudh later shared photographs from two ceremonies on Instagram, captioning the post, “My once in a lifetime, for a lifetime 11.11.” Kavya is the daughter of Sun Group chairman Kalanithi Maran and is widely recognised for her association with Sunrisers Hyderabad. Her candid reactions during IPL matches frequently attract attention on social media. Anirudh and Kavya’s wedding looks
 For the wedding celebrations, Kavya Maran wore a blush-pink floor-length lehenga featuring intricate floral embroidery, sequins and beadwork. She completed the look with a fitted short-sleeved blouse. Join conversation

 Anirudh Ravichander coordinated with her in an ivory-beige traditional outfit featuring a blush-pink silk shirt, matching veshti and an embroidered jacket. Layered necklaces and beige suede loafers completed his look.  Anirudh recently composed the music for Nelson's ‘Jailer 2’, starring Rajinikanth . The composer has several projects lined up, including Rajinikanth's ‘Dharman’, ‘Dare Devil’, ‘Indian 3’, Kamal Haasan's ‘Sandiyar’, Allu Arjun's ‘AA23’ and STR's ‘Arasan’.
